readings: Linking each examination to its patient by `ID` (dropping examinations with no matching patient), work per examination: take each examination's own `aCL IgM` value along with its patient's `ID` and `SEX`. Find the overall mean of these per-examination values and each one's deviation from that overall mean. Then, within each sex (exact text match, so a blank sex is its own group and a missing sex matches nothing), average those deviations. Keep only the per-examination values whose deviation is above their sex's average deviation, and show the top 10 by how far above it they are, largest first (missing last): patient `ID`, `SEX`, the `aCL IgM` value, its deviation from the overall mean, and how far that deviation exceeds the sex's average deviation. All averages ignore missing values; don't round.
queries:
WITH base AS (
    SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(igm) AS m FROM base
),
dev AS (
    SELECT b.ID, b.SEX, b.igm, b.igm - o.m AS deviation
    FROM base b, overall o
),
sexavg AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(deviation) AS avg_dev
    FROM dev
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.deviation, d.deviation - s.avg_dev AS excess
FROM dev d
JOIN sexavg s ON s.SEX = d.SEX
WHERE d.deviation > s.avg_dev
ORDER BY excess DESC
LIMIT 10;
